items.title: Father Al Lewis Interview, 1972-02-21
items.q: The interviewee does not mention John Lama; the name is introduced by Speaker_03 in a question/statement ('John Lama's, the Big 25?') which the interviewee does not directly address or confirm involvement with.

ctx.x: No, it was right behind Krause on Corset Street, where they cut that annexed
trope. Oh, you're talking about Abbeville and Franca. Yeah. John Lama's, the Big 25? Yeah, 225. Well you never did play as a piece on it.

No, I played for Dog House and I played, when that closed down I went down the next block with Octave Crosby, Joe Harris. You remember Octave Crosby that died? Yeah. Yeah, down the next block. We were working for Elie Groeschel, you know where the Dog House we started working for. Who's the Dog House? The one on? They had it down there and the next block on Corset and Bindleland and then they moved it out there on North Ramport. I believe it was Ramport or St. Claude they called it. You understand? Yeah, I…
